items.title: Lidocaine trigger-point injection beat dry needling for 1-hour ED pain relief
items.evidence_note: Challenge pick: chosen to test usual physio practice. Single small ED trial in acute myofascial low back pain; no placebo arm and short follow-up.
items.confidence_note: Numbers and design were clearly reported in the full text.
items.impact_line: This supports saying trigger-point injection may give faster short-term relief than dry needling in the ED, but the comparison is unblinded and preliminary.
summary: Trigger-point injection reduced pain more than dry needling over the first hour.
65.2% in the dry-needling group needed rescue fentanyl; 0% in the injection group.
No procedure-related adverse events were reported during the ED stay.

pico.p: Adults with acute myofascial low back pain in an emergency department
pico.o: Short-term pain reduction and rescue analgesic use

limits: Single centre
Open label
No long-term follow-up
No placebo or saline control
Baseline imbalances in pain duration, temperature, and oxygen saturation
items.bottom_line: In this small, open-label ED trial, lidocaine trigger-point injection gave greater short-term pain relief than dry needling and reduced rescue fentanyl use, but baseline imbalance, no blinding, and no placebo arm limit certainty.

methods.setting: Emergency department, Atatürk University Faculty of Medicine Research Hospital, Türkiye
methods.participants: Adults with acute myofascial low back pain
methods.primary_outcome: Between-group difference in percentage pain reduction at 30 minutes

results.detail: Primary outcome was %ΔNRS-30; adjusted analysis also favoured injection, 47.1 percentage points greater reduction.
Rescue fentanyl was given only after the final pain score; the dry-needling group needed it much more often.
Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, hypotension, bleeding, and hematoma were each 0 in both groups during the observation window.

how_to_apply: If choosing between these two procedures in the ED, injection may give faster pain relief.
Do not treat this as proof that lidocaine is superior in general.
Expect the result to be less certain in non-ED, chronic, or longer-term care.
Monitor for adverse events, but this study was too small to assess rare harms.

weaknesses: Large baseline imbalance in pain duration

items.title: ACL rehab guideline: early motion, loading and criteria-based progression
items.evidence_note: Broad guideline; many recommendations rely on low-certainty evidence and expert consensus.
items.confidence_note: Methods and recommendations are explicit in full text.
items.impact_line: Use criteria-based, early active rehabilitation; be cautious about modalities and return-to-sport claims.
summary: 140 RCTs informed the guideline, but most studies had some concerns or high risk of bias.
Early motion, progressive weight-bearing and exercise are the backbone of rehab after isolated ACLR.
Several adjuncts may help short-term symptoms, but many effects are small, conflicting or very low certainty.
Return-to-running and return-to-sport criteria are proposed, but the paper says they are not fully validated.
